text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Medical Council reconsidering relations with the media after complaint by The Times that public and press not informed of council decisions.

- Broadcasting Authority has ordered the television station of the opposition Malta Labour Party to be impartial during the election campaign, in line with the law. The MLP, the only political party to have a television station, says authority is unjustified. It complains that the state broadcasting favours the ruling Nationalists.
- Inflation expected to drop to three percent from nearly four percent last year.

- EU Intergovernmental Conference expected to end in June. Prime Minister Eddie Fenech Adami tells party supporters that Irish Prime Minister John Bruton had phoned him to say the current EU inter-governmental conference was expected to be over by June. Malta has been promised talks on EU membership six months after the end of the conference.
